$comment: How the canvas behaves on a desk, a tablet and a phone: one row per rule. A row is the same everywhere (`value`), or differs by form (desk, tablet, phone), by pointer (mouse, pen, touch), by operating system (computer, mobile), by browser engine (webkit, chromium, other) or by GPU class (big, small, phone): `by` says which, and the row has one value per column. `says` is the rule in words. TypeScript reads this file through device/rules.ts; the engine's editor crate reads the same file. The board 'The rules, per device' on the Decks Studio canvas is this table in words.

press.slop-px.says: How far a press may move on the screen before it means to move.

tap.ms.says: A press let go within this long, and within tap.px of where it landed, is a tap.

tap.px.says: A finger that has gone this far on the screen is a pan or a carry, not a tap.

tap.second-ms.says: A second tap on the same item within this long is a double tap.

tap.second-on-item.says: A double tap on an item opens its words on a desk; on touch a selected card becomes active, its page taking the pointer until a tap outside.

tap.bare-second-ms.says: Two taps on bare canvas this close in time make a note there.

tap.bare-second-px.says: And this close on the screen.

click.after-pan-ms.says: A double-click this soon after the camera was dragged is the end of a pan, not a double-click.

click.after-make-ms.says: A double-click this soon after a tool made an item is that click's second press.

hold.ms.says: A press held still this long is a hold.

hold.on-item.says: A hold on an item opens its menu with a preview on touch; on a desk the right button does.

hold.on-bare.says: A hold on bare canvas starts selecting on touch: the finger drags a marquee from there.

touch.carry-min-px.says: A finger on an item at least this big on the screen both ways carries it, selected or not, and the hold menu it opens turns into a carry once it moves; on a smaller one it pans the canvas, so a canvas far out and full of items can still be moved.

hover.outline.says: An outline follows the pointer in edit mode on a desk; touch has no hover.

press.on-live-page.says: A press on a live card's page goes to the page on a desk (but on its title or edge); on touch a cover takes it until the card is active, so a tap selects and a drag moves.

drag.copy-with-alt.says: Alt while dragging copies; a finger has no Alt.

pen.on-bare.says: A Pencil on bare canvas with the select tool turns the pen on and starts the stroke; the palm is ignored.

handle.size-px.says: A resize handle as drawn, on the screen.

handle.shape.says: Squares under a pointer, dots under a finger.

handle.which.says: Eight handles on a desk, the four corners on touch.

handle.reach-px.says: How wide a handle answers a press, whatever it is drawn: a finger's width on touch.

handle.min-px.says: An item smaller than this on the screen, both ways, shows no handles.

handle.size-label.says: The width × height label under a selection.

arrow.anchors.says: The arrow anchors round a selected item.

arrow.end-px.says: A selected arrow's end handle as drawn: bigger under a finger.

arrow.bend-px.says: A selected arrow's middle handle, that bends it, as drawn.

arrow.anchor-out-px.says: How far outside the item an anchor sits.

line.reach-px.says: How far a press reaches a thin line, on the screen: wider for a finger.

edge.out-px.says: How far outside a card its edge answers a resize.

snap.px.says: A drag snaps to edges and centres within this far, on every form.

snap.by-pointer.says: Which pointers snap: all of them.

snap.reading-gap-px.says: Boards snap to this gap from their neighbours.

arrow.join-px.says: An arrow's end joins an item within this far.

arrow.side-px.says: Within this far of a side, the end keeps to that side.

arrow.slide-px.says: An end slides along its side within this far.

drop.near-px.says: Drop slots within this far of the pointer are drawn dashed; the one under it solid.

glide.ms.says: What a drop moved glides to where it lands over this long.

pill.place.says: The item's pill goes above or below on a desk, re-chosen when the item changes; on touch always below, placed once, hidden while dragging.

nudge.px.says: An arrow key moves the selection this far.

duplicate.offset-px.says: A duplicate lands this far down and right.

pan.by.says: Who moves the camera for a pan while the pointer is down: the browser's own scroll on a desk; on touch the canvas, from every finger on it, so the pan, its coast and a pinch are one owner's and nothing is handed over at the lift.

coast.by.says: Who carries a pan on after the lift: the trackpad's momentum on a desk; on touch our coast, so a finger landing mid-coast is an ordinary press and a pinch works at once.

coast.tau-ms.says: Our coast loses about two thirds of its speed in this long, as an iOS list does: a flick glides about a second and a half.

pinch.travel-px.says: A trackpad pinch (Ctrl and the wheel, as Chrome sends it): wheel units per e-fold of the zoom, each event held to ×1.3.

wheel.travel-px.says: ⌘ and a mouse wheel: wheel units per e-fold of the zoom, each event held to ×1.3.

live.zoom.says: Below this zoom every item is its picture.

picture.fade-ms.says: A sharper picture cross-fades over the one it replaces in this long.

layers.says: Which items go on layers of their own while the camera moves: none in WebKit; each awake item in a zoom and the world in a pan elsewhere.

moving.says: What an awake item shows while the camera moves: in WebKit its picture, since Safari redraws every awake page at each step of a zoom on the canvas's one thread; elsewhere its live page.

tools.says: The tools: a floating column on a desk and a tablet, a row above the dock on a phone.

properties.says: The properties: a floating panel, a popover by the selection, a sheet from the bottom over the composer.

properties.opens.says: Open whenever something is selected on a desk; from the pill or the hold menu on touch.

conversation.says: The conversation: the side panel, or a sheet from the pill on a phone.

awake.says: How many items are live at once besides the selected one, by kind, and how many let go are kept: by operating system, since a mobile one gives a page one thread and a hard memory ceiling.

files.live.says: How many files near the window show live.

pictures.says: The picture sizes a card can have and the memory they may take, by GPU class.
